key_insight: Particle trapping in a time-periodic vortex is lost through a saddle-node bifurcation when outward inertia overcomes inward thermophoretic migration.
engineering_relevance: This identifies a tunable threshold for designing thermal-flow systems that either retain or release inertial particles by adjusting forcing, temperature gradients, or particle properties.
method: Derived a small-Stokes-number, cycle-averaged radial migration model from the particle equations of motion.
Analyzed fixed points of the reduced radial dynamics to identify stable trapping states and separatrices.
Used phase portraits, bifurcation diagrams, and asymptotic analysis to confirm saddle-node loss of trapping and critical slowing down.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports analytical phase-portrait and bifurcation analysis, plus additional tests with multiple velocity and temperature profiles showing the mechanism is robust across profiles.
watch_item: The reduction relies on a small-Stokes-number, cycle-averaged model, so behavior outside that asymptotic regime may require full trajectory simulation.
paper_title: Trapping-loss transition via a saddle-node bifurcation in thermophoretic particle transport driven by a time-periodic vortex
